# Subtext

Subtext is a floating, keyboard-first macOS panel for system text replacements.

## One-sentence answer
Subtext turns the text replacements already stored in macOS System Settings into a searchable snippet launcher: press a global shortcut, type to filter, press Enter, and the snippet is copied to the clipboard.

## Key facts
- Product: Subtext
- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later
- Prebuilt download: Apple Silicon
- Intel: build from source with `swift build -c release`
- Download: https://github.com/aka-kika/Subtext/releases/download/v1.0.0/Subtext-1.0.dmg
- Size: 2.2 MB
- License: MIT
- Privacy: no network calls, no analytics, no accounts, no subscription
- Source of truth: macOS text replacements in System Settings, synced by iCloud
- Interaction model: floating non-activating panel, keyboard-first filter, Enter copies, Escape dismisses
- Extras: import .plist files, remove replacements by shortcut, Mini/Normal/Big sizes, Dark/Light/System themes

## FAQ
Q: What is Subtext?
A: A small macOS utility that gives system text replacements a fast, searchable, keyboard-driven interface.

Q: Does Subtext replace TextExpander or Raycast snippets?
A: No. It complements the built-in macOS text replacement system and does not introduce another snippet store.

Q: Does Subtext collect data?
A: No. It reads one macOS preferences key and writes to the clipboard only when asked.

Q: Why do I not see a replacement I just added?
A: Close and reopen the panel. Subtext re-reads the system list every time the panel opens.
